open_points.subject: State 0 acceptance
open_points.text: “Reopened by the owner on 2026-10-27” and “State 0 closes again when its question rounds are clear; the owner then accepts it as a whole,” while Open questions says “None open.”
open_points.question: Has the current post-R0-71 text been accepted as a whole and closed, or is it still an unaccepted reopened draft?
options: Accept and close the current whole
Keep it reopened pending an explicit whole-document acceptance
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as reopened and not yet accepted as a whole.

open_points.subject: Authority of R0-45
open_points.text: “R0-45 — Object at creation, edited with the card, covered by the owner interface (proposed to the owner 2026-10-27 after round 3 T8, T11, T12, no objection)”
open_points.question: Does “no objection” make R0-45 an accepted owner decision, or is explicit acceptance still required?
options: Treat R0-45 as accepted
Leave R0-45 proposed until explicitly accepted
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as accepted because later text relies on it.

open_points.subject: Meaning of Registry frontend in earlier decisions
open_points.text: “In decisions before R0-24, ‘the Registry frontend’ reads ‘the owner interface’” conflicts with R0-13’s narrowing: “both are retired,” referring to “The Registry frontend and `onboard_object`.”
open_points.question: Does the global substitution apply to R0-13, which would say the owner interface is retired, or does “Registry frontend” there continue to mean only the retired old frontend?
options: Exclude retirement passages from the substitution
Apply the substitution and revise R0-13’s retirement wording
open_points.default_guess: Treat R0-13 as retiring only the old frontend, not the owner interface.

open_points.subject: Owner choice versus agent project selection
open_points.text: The Product statement says Registry “lets the owner choose the project the agent works on,” while R0-46 allows the agent to name and compare any project in its granted set and makes the active project only “the default when the agent names none.”
open_points.question: May an agent select any granted project per operation, or must it operate only on the active project chosen by the owner?
options: Any granted project may be named; active is only a default
Only the owner-selected active project may be used
open_points.default_guess: Allow any granted project and treat the active project as a default only.

open_points.subject: Authentication of the sign-in request
open_points.text: “Every request on either is authenticated; anything not authenticated is refused” and “No operation of Registry answers an unauthenticated caller,” while “The owner signs in to the owner interface with the owner credential.”
open_points.question: Which unauthenticated owner-interface requests, at minimum the sign-in form and credential submission, are allowed to receive an answer?
options: Declare a narrow unauthenticated sign-in exception
Require an external authentication layer before every Registry request
open_points.default_guess: Allow only the sign-in form and sign-in submission without an existing owner session.

open_points.subject: Export required for migration
open_points.text: “The owner exports the chosen source and uploads the export through the owner interface,” but Primary actions defines import and no action that exports a source instance.
open_points.question: What named actor or system produces the VPS or test-rig export, with what observable output and failures?
options: Add a Registry export action on each source instance
Name an external migration/export tool and exclude it from Registry
open_points.default_guess: Add an owner-authenticated export action to the source Registry instance.

open_points.subject: Repeated session registration
open_points.text: The register action outputs “the session Registry knows, with no granted project,” while R0-53 says “registering a session already registered returns it unchanged.”
open_points.question: What does registration return when the named session already exists with grants, an active project or a pending request?
options: Return the existing session unchanged with its existing access
Refuse duplicate registration
Reset the existing session to empty access
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing session unchanged, including its current access state.

open_points.subject: Rooms of an anonymised project
open_points.text: R0-62 says an anonymised project keeps “its id, status and artifact pointers and nothing else,” but `list rooms` specifies only that an unknown project is refused and gives no result for an anonymised project.
open_points.question: What does `list rooms` return for an anonymised project whose rooms were removed?
options: Return an erased-project refusal
Return an empty room list
Return not found
open_points.default_guess: Return an erased-project refusal, matching project, context and agent-projection reads.

open_points.subject: Agent projection personal-data guarantee
open_points.text: The projection promises “no … other personal value,” but R0-68 keeps room names and artifact pointers, says “Registry does not inspect these values,” and Primary actions lets the agent add rooms and publish pointers.
open_points.question: How can Registry guarantee that no personal value reaches an agent when uninspected room names, `uri`, `payload_ref` and digest values are returned to agents and may be written by owners, services or other agent sessions?
options: Make the rule an explicit trust assumption rather than a Registry guarantee
Validate or structurally constrain these returned values
Remove free-text room names and pointer values from the agent projection
open_points.default_guess: State an explicit trusted-input invariant and classify a violation as outside Registry’s guarantees.

open_points.subject: Personal data retained in anonymised artifact pointers
open_points.text: R0-62 keeps artifact pointers after anonymisation, R0-71 says the anonymised project “holds no personal value,” and R0-33/R0-68 say Registry never inspects pointer content.
open_points.question: What establishes that retained `uri`, `payload_ref` and digest values contain no personal or re-identifying information before anonymisation succeeds?
options: Require owner confirmation that every retained pointer is safe
Remove or redact unsafe pointer fields
Treat pointer safety as an external governance assertion and narrow the guarantee
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner’s anonymisation confirmation to assert that retained pointers are non-identifying.

open_points.subject: Customer erasure and surviving customer_ref links
open_points.text: R0-52 says “the personal data and the links that identify a person are removed,” while R0-06 and R0-67 say projects keep naming the erased Customer by its surviving identity.
open_points.question: Does erasing customer contact data also remove project `customer_ref` links that can identify the customer through another service, or are those links explicitly allowed to survive?
options: Remove the project-to-customer links
Keep the links only after an explicit non-reidentification determination
Always keep `customer_ref` links and narrow R0-52
open_points.default_guess: Keep the links only if governance establishes that the surviving reference cannot re-identify the person.

open_points.subject: Audit event coverage
open_points.text: R0-58 records “only significant changes of state: changes to projects and customer records, granting and revoking an agent session’s projects, restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations.”
open_points.question: Does the audit log include room creation, artifact publication or withdrawal, session registration, active-project changes, access requests and answers, relationship end or resume, imports, and failed changes, or is the stated list exhaustive?
options: Treat the stated categories as exhaustive
Audit every accepted state-changing primary action
Declare an explicit event-by-event inclusion table
open_points.default_guess: Use an explicit event table and include every accepted state-changing primary action except pending access-request text changes and ordinary agent calls.

open_points.subject: Session access version and stale changes
open_points.text: `read the session’s access` returns “the access version,” while R0-29 says “Every change … made against an older revision is refused,” but no action says which access changes move the version or which owner actions must present it.
open_points.question: Which events increment the access version, and must grant, revoke, active-project change, request replacement and request answer supply the version they were made against?
options: Move it on every session-access or pending-request change and require it for owner mutations
Move it only when grants or active project change
Return a version for observation only, without stale-write enforcement
open_points.default_guess: Move it on every change to grants, active project or pending request, and require it for owner mutations.

open_points.subject: Repeated grants and active-project changes
open_points.text: “the project joins the session’s granted set” and “the session’s active project changes,” with no output or failure for granting an already-granted project or selecting the already-active project.
open_points.question: Are these repeated access changes refused, returned unchanged, or accepted while moving the access version and audit log?
options: Return unchanged without moving the version
Accept and move the version
Refuse as an invalid transition
open_points.default_guess: Return unchanged without moving the access version or writing a change audit entry.

open_points.subject: Repeated restriction transitions
open_points.text: “restrict or lift a restriction on a customer” defines unknown or erased as failures but is silent about restricting an already restricted customer or lifting a customer that is not restricted.
open_points.question: What are the observable result, revision effect and audit effect of repeated restriction or lift requests?
options: Return unchanged without moving the revision
Accept and move the revision
Refuse the invalid transition
open_points.default_guess: Return unchanged without moving the revision or logging a state change.

open_points.subject: Relationship end date and repeated transitions
open_points.text: The action outputs “The Customer marked as ended on that date, or the mark cleared” but does not say whether the date is supplied by the owner or generated by Registry, nor what happens when ending an already-ended relationship or resuming one that is not ended.
open_points.question: Where does the relationship-end date come from, and what are the result, revision and audit effects of repeated end or resume requests?
options: Owner supplies the date; repeated transitions are unchanged
Registry records its current date; repeated transitions are unchanged
Repeated transitions are refused
open_points.default_guess: Let the owner supply the effective date and make repeated transitions unchanged.

open_points.subject: Audit erasure with a future cutoff
open_points.text: The action says “every entry older than the date the owner gives is gone; the erasure leaves an entry of its own naming the date.”
open_points.question: If the owner gives a future cutoff, the newly written erasure entry is itself older than that cutoff; is the date refused, is the new entry exempt, or is it immediately erased?
options: Refuse cutoffs later than the operation time
Exempt the erasure’s own entry from its cutoff
Apply the cutoff again and erase the new entry
open_points.default_guess: Refuse a cutoff later than the operation time.

open_points.subject: Imported identities versus separate identity spaces
open_points.text: Test instances “hold their own identity space,” R0-21 says a test instance “never shares production’s identity space,” while import “keeps every identity” and leaves the source instance holding the same ids after production accepts them.
open_points.question: After import, are identical textual ids allowed to remain in both source and production, and if so what exactly makes their identity spaces distinct?
options: Identity is scoped by instance even when textual ids match
A successful import retires or removes the source identities
Production remaps ids despite the keep-identity promise
open_points.default_guess: Scope identity by instance and allow matching textual ids, with production designated authoritative.
